paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God did the reconciling, and He did it first. Paul writes that God "reconciled us to Himself through Christ," and that He was "not counting men’s trespasses against them" (2 Corinthians 5:18-19). You don't climb your way back to God one good batch at a time, because He made the way, and the way is Jesus.

And look at what that does to a person. "Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!" (2 Corinthians 5:17). Christ's love is what pushes Paul, because One died for all so that those who live "should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again" (2 Corinthians 5:14-15). I went into that drawer worn out and came out sharp, so I'm telling you, new is REAL.

Now here's where it gets personal, baker. God has committed the message of reconciliation to us, so we are "ambassadors for Christ" (2 Corinthians 5:19-20). The appeal is still going out: "Be reconciled to God." And Paul says it's not a someday thing, because "now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!" (2 Corinthians 6:2). So don't receive God's grace in vain, friend: take it, live in it, and hand it to somebody else.
